Class EntityLimit

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.entities.BaseID<Integer>
grafiosch.entities.ProposeTransientTransfer
grafiosch.entities.Auditable
grafiosch.entities.EntityLimit
All Implemented Interfaces:
AdminEntity, Serializable
@Entity public class EntityLimit extends Auditable implements AdminEntity, Serializable
One configured anti-flooding limit. Replaces the gt.max.* / gt.limit.day.* / g.limit.day.* rows of globalparameters and the former user_entity_change_limit table with a single, role- and user-aware configuration table.

The first five columns form the limit key (see LimitKey); idRole and idUser are mutually exclusive and say who the row applies to. Both null makes it the ALL default row of that key. The resolver consults a user row first, then the row of the user's most privileged role, then the ALL row, and treats a key with no row at all as unlimited.

The validation rule for limitValue is deliberately not a column: it belongs to the key and lives in the limit key registry, so a per-role or per-user override is validated exactly like the ALL default. This differs from globalparameters, where the rule sits on the row.

    • getLimitTypeKey

      public String getLimitTypeKey()
      Translation key under which the limit type is displayed. The enum constant name alone cannot serve as the key: MAX, ALL and TENANT are already taken by unrelated texts, so every constant of the three limit enums is prefixed with its enum name.
      Returns:
      for example LIMIT_TYPE_DAY_CUD
